brl_wolves.description:
You'll forgive me if I don't stand. Deathguard Rennick, and this gate is mine from dusk until whenever somebody remembers to relieve me.

The Bleak Worgs have been coming up the Deathknell road after dark. Not at us yet - at the edges, the way a thing does when it is working out whether we are worth the trouble. Nobody in Brill has been bitten. The living would call that luck. I have stood at a gate long enough to call it a question being asked.

Go down into Nightmare Vale and answer it. Thin the pack, and leave enough of a mess that the rest of them draw the right conclusion.
brl_wolves.accept_text: Take the west road down to the Vale. Bring me the count and I'll pretend I'm not worried.
brl_wolves.turn_in_text:
Good. That's the answer I wanted them to have.

Brill sleeps lighter than it admits, friend. Take something out of the crate - nobody in there is using it.

brl_nightmare.description:
One more thing, since you came back with your arms attached.

Nobody has walked the lower road through Nightmare Vale since the worgs settled in. I have three patrol rosters on this post and every one of them says the same word about what is down there, and the word is 'something'. You cannot set a watch against something. You cannot tell a frightened farmer anything useful about something.

Walk it. End to end, the whole length, and look properly at the bottom of it. Then come back and give me a noun.
brl_nightmare.accept_text: South-west of the Cold Hearth road, past the Deathknell gate, where the road goes into the trees. Don't dawdle.
brl_nightmare.turn_in_text:
Quiet. You're certain.

I like quiet less than you'd think. Quiet is what a place sounds like when whatever lives there has already seen you and decided there's no hurry.

brl_glades.description:
Stop there. You see that? Out past the posts, in the long grass - that drifting about.

Wretched Zombies out of the western glades. They're slow, they're stupid, and I'll say it plain because the Deathguard won't: they mean nothing by it. There's no malice left in one of those. They just wander, and lately they've been wandering at my gate.

I have a quota of corpses I'm willing to step over on my way to this post, and it has been exceeded. Go and put them down properly, which is more mercy than they'd get from anyone else on this road.
brl_glades.accept_text: Out along the road west. Put them down and I'll let you back in without a lecture.
brl_glades.turn_in_text:
That's the road clear. I was getting a crick in my neck from all the stepping over.

They'll come back eventually. They always do. But not this week, and this week is what I'm paid for.

brl_news_landing.description:
Wexley. Town crier, Brill, and the first man in this town to know anything - a position I hold by effort, not by luck.

Which is why it galls me to be standing here repeating a rumour I cannot confirm. They are saying the zeppelin tower east of here, out at the Landing, is open and taking passengers. Goblins, ropes, the whole swaying business of it. If that's true, it is the biggest thing to happen to this town since the Dark Lady took the Undercity, and I will not be the last man in Brill to say so out loud.

Go east and look at it with your own eyes. I'll not cry a thing I haven't had confirmed.
brl_news_landing.accept_text: East along the high road, then south. The tower is a tangle of ropes and goblin cursing. Go and tell me if it's real.
brl_news_landing.turn_in_text:
Real. Real, and open for custom!

I shall cry it from the steps within the hour, and I shall mention that I had it confirmed before anyone. Thank you - genuinely. A crier is only ever as good as the man he sent to check.

brl_news_ruins.description:
The Landing is a story about commerce. This one is a story about us, and I'd rather have it right.

South of the tower are the Ruins of Lordaeron - the old capital, what's left of it, and the gate down into the Undercity. Every week somebody comes up that road with a tale: that the throne room's been cleared, that there are lights in the upper halls, that something's moved in where the Menethil line used to sit.

I need the approach walked by someone who will tell me what they actually saw rather than what makes a better evening at the inn. Go and see who is still home.
brl_news_ruins.accept_text: South of the Landing, along the road the Dark Lady took. Don't linger - the ghosts up there remember being important.
brl_news_ruins.turn_in_text:
Mm. That matches two of the four versions I've been told, which is about as close to truth as this town gets.

I'll cry the careful version. People think a crier's job is noise. It's mostly deciding what not to say.

brl_grael_pumpkins.description:
Keep your voice down, the Apothecary's just through there and he does not like to be interrupted by errands he considers beneath the work.

Grael. Assistant, which in this building means I fetch. What I need fetched are the pumpkins out of the Solliden fields - swollen things, grey-green, gone soft at the shoulder. They ferment into the finest reagent base we have, and nothing else in Tirisfal does it half as well.

The Grain Threshers are growing them and the Grain Threshers hit back, which is precisely why I am standing here asking you instead of walking out there myself. Uncracked, please. I am very particular about cracks.
brl_grael_pumpkins.accept_text: The threshers in the Solliden fields carry them. Uncracked. I'll know.
brl_grael_pumpkins.turn_in_text:
Oh, those are lovely. Not a split in them.

Don't tell the Apothecary how pleased I am. He thinks enthusiasm is a symptom.

brl_grael_pearls.description:
Another one, if you have the stomach for the smell of the bay.

The Vile Fin murlocs out on the Whispering Shore wear little salt-pearls - the oracles do, specifically, the ones that stand at the back and make the noise. Ground fine, they settle a plague draught that would otherwise take the lining out of a person. We use a great deal of it.

I have no idea what the murlocs want them for. I asked, once, in the way you ask a murloc things, and I came away wet and no wiser. Whatever it means to them, they can spare some.
brl_grael_pearls.accept_text: North-west, where the bay meets the dead marsh. The little oracles. Don't scratch them.
brl_grael_pearls.turn_in_text:
Perfect. Look at the lustre on that - you can see why they bother.

I do sometimes wonder whether we're taking something from them that matters. Then I grind it up, and the wondering passes.

brl_grael_iceshard.description:
Last errand, and the cold one, so I've saved it for someone who looked like they could take a walk in bad weather.

Brightwater Lake sheds shards of black ice all year - summer, winter, makes no difference, which should tell you something about that water. The shades along the shore pick them up and carry them about like keepsakes. I've watched one hold a shard for an hour and do nothing with it at all.

We use them for cold-fixing, which keeps a reagent from turning while it sits. Bring me what the shades and the drowned are carrying. And wear gloves - I am not being delicate, that ice takes fingers.
brl_grael_iceshard.accept_text: Eastern Tirisfal, Brightwater Lake. The shades and the drowned carry fragments. Gloves.
brl_grael_iceshard.turn_in_text:
Still cold. They always are, hours later, no matter what you wrap them in.

Thank you. Go and stand near the fire a while - you've gone the colour of the lake.

brl_hollis_robbers.description:
Thirty years I've dug in this ground. Dug for the living when it was the living we buried, and dug for whatever we are now, and I'll tell you the one thing both have in common: a grave is a promise. You put a person in the earth and the earth keeps them.

Somebody's been breaking that promise up at Garren's Haunt. Rot Hide gnolls - graverobbers, working the old plots, and doing it badly. They take what's valuable and leave the rest lying out in the wrong arrangement. Not scattered. Arranged. I don't like that at all.

And here's the part that has me in a temper: they're using my shovels. Stolen out of this very yard. Put them in the ground with them.
brl_hollis_robbers.accept_text: Up at Garren's Haunt. They use shovels. I recognise the shovels. They're mine.
brl_hollis_robbers.turn_in_text:
And my shovels back. Chipped, but back.

You'd think a man in my condition would have made his peace with bodies being moved about. Turns out that's precisely why I haven't.

brl_hollis_relics.description:
Now the other half of it, and this is the half that actually matters to me.

Whatever those gnolls lifted is still out there, and the crypt wights in the Agamand vault have been at the same work for longer. Rings. Seals. Little carved things an Agamand was buried holding, because somebody who loved them thought they ought to have it.

I don't want it sold and I don't want it kept. I want it back in the ground. I've dug for this family since before the plague and I'd like the ledger to balance before I stop. Bring me what you find, and bring all of it - I'll know the shape of a gap.
brl_hollis_relics.accept_text: The wights in the Agamand crypt and the robbers at Garren's Haunt carry the best of it. And no keeping any.
brl_hollis_relics.turn_in_text:
Every piece. I did wonder.

I'll put these back tonight, properly, with the right names over them. It won't matter to the Agamands. It matters to the ground, and it matters to me, and that'll do.

brl_meryl_orders.description:
You're not from the Deathguard. Good. I'll say this once and quietly.

My name is Meryl Ashdown and my brother is in the Scarlet Crusade. He marched off while he was still breathing and I stopped being able to follow it after that. I don't know if he's alive. I don't know if he's still himself - you hear what the Crusade does to a man's thinking, and he was never the steadiest of us.

The recruits at the Crusader Outpost carry their orders on them. Convert rosters, postings, names. Somewhere in that paper is whether he is still listed. I'm not going to ask how you get them, and I'd rather you didn't tell me. But if you meet a thin man with our mother's jaw - please.
brl_meryl_orders.accept_text: The Crusader Outpost, west of the Solliden farms. Please. And don't hurt him if you meet him.
brl_meryl_orders.turn_in_text:
[She reads each sheet twice before she sets it down.]

He isn't here. Not listed, not struck off, not anywhere in this. Which means nothing, and I'll be honest with you - nothing is better than what I was braced for.

Thank you. You're the first person in three years to come back to me with an answer instead of a kindness.

brl_nettles_crows.description:
Them bats. Out over the glades, the big grey ones. You see them?

They're the crows. Same crows that took my barley every autumn for forty years, and don't you start - I know what people in town say about Old Nettles and his crows. I know what they turned into, and I know what I turned into, and I notice nobody wants to discuss the second one.

Nothing grows in that field now. Nothing has grown there since before the plague. I'm aware. But a man either keeps the pact he made with his land or he doesn't, and I'm not having the principle of the thing decided by a bat. Go and see them off.
brl_nettles_crows.accept_text: Out in the glades, the big grey ones. They've had my crop and my patience.
brl_nettles_crows.turn_in_text:
Hah! That's them told.

Field's still dead. I'm still dead. But that's a proper field with a proper crop of nothing in it, and it's mine, and the birds can keep off it.

brl_pruit_straw.description:
Careful of the posts. I've only just got that one standing straight.

I tend the scarecrows on Brill's plots - have done since there were crops worth guarding, and I've kept at it since there weren't. Somebody has to. A field with a scarecrow in it is a field somebody still means something by.

The Rotting Dead come in off the glades and knock them flat, and that I could live with. What I can't live with is what they do after. They lean on the posts. They stay there. And when you come out in the morning there's a shape up on the frame that is not straw and not mine, and I have to take it down, and I have to decide what to do with it. I'd like that to stop.
brl_pruit_straw.accept_text: Out in the plots. Don't bring them back here - I'll make do with straw.
brl_pruit_straw.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I mean that.

I'll re-stuff the frames this evening and they'll be scarecrows again. Just straw and a coat. That's all they were ever supposed to be.

brl_ohmsted_toll.description:
The bell goes once a day, at dusk. One stroke, for everyone Brightwater Lake has kept.

It isn't a ceremony and the Apothecary has told me more than once that it isn't useful. He's right. It's a habit I had when I was breathing and it's a habit I have now, and I've lost enough else that I'd rather not examine that one too closely.

Here's the trouble. For the last month or so, when I ring it - the lake rings back. The Drowned Wretches come up out of the shallows and they make a sound that is not an echo, and they keep making it after I've stopped. I'd like them quiet. I'd like to be able to ring for them without them answering.
brl_ohmsted_toll.accept_text: East past Brill, the big lake on the north side. They rise at dusk and wail.
brl_ohmsted_toll.turn_in_text:
[He listens for a long moment, head tilted toward the water.]

Nothing. Just the bell, and then the bell stopping.

I'll ring for them tomorrow as well. It's only right. But I'd rather do the remembering on my own, thank you.

brl_ohmsted_shades.description:
The wretches in the water were one thing. The shades along the shore are another, and I've been putting off asking.

When the bell goes, they weep. Not an echo of it - their own sound, starting after mine and going on long after. I have heard a great many terrible things since I stopped breathing and that is the worst of them, because it is almost grief and it is not quite.

I don't know what's left in a shade. Perhaps nothing, and it's only the shape of mourning with no one inside it. Either way I'd like them stilled. If there IS someone in there, then they've been standing on a cold shore crying at a bell for years, and that's reason enough on its own.
brl_ohmsted_shades.accept_text: Same lake. Along the shore, not in it. They're rather high-handed about it.
brl_ohmsted_shades.turn_in_text:
Still. All of them.

I'll keep ringing. Somebody has to, and now the only thing that answers is the water, which is how it ought to be.

brl_joss_home.description:
You'll have to be patient with me. I'm new to this - the waking up, I mean. Weeks, not years, and most of it won't sit still in my head.

Here's what I have. A stable with a bad door. A paddock gone over with thistle. A farmhouse, and a woman in it who made bread on a Thursday, and I can smell that more clearly than I can remember her face, which seems a poor trade.

Balnir, I think it was called. South of the east road. I can't go - I've tried twice and turned back both times, and I'd rather not explain why. Walk the place for me. Tell me what's still standing. I'd like to know whether I'm remembering a home or inventing one.
brl_joss_home.accept_text: Balnir, I think they called it. South of the east road. Look at the farmhouse for me.
brl_joss_home.turn_in_text:
The stable door. You're sure about the stable door - hanging off the one hinge, the bottom one.

Then it was real. I wasn't sure, and nobody could tell me, and now I am.

I'm not going to go and look. I want to leave it where you put it, standing, with the door wrong. Thank you for that.

brl_ilvessa_cargo.description:
Finally, somebody competent-looking. Ilvessa - I keep the stall at the end, the one with the good lacquer and no customers.

My shipment came down from the Undercity on the zeppelin and never reached this square. Scavengers took it on the road, picked the crates open, and scattered what they didn't fancy. That's irritating. What's dangerous is that they got away with it, because the next shipment comes in on the same schedule down the same road, and scavengers can count.

Get my crates back. I don't particularly need what's in them. I need it to have cost somebody something, before the whole road decides my stall is a seasonal harvest.
brl_ilvessa_cargo.accept_text: Ragged scavengers along the eastern road. They steal anything that glints.
brl_ilvessa_cargo.turn_in_text:
Half the lacquerware is cracked and one of the bolts of cloth has been used as bedding. Lovely.

But it came back, and they know it came back. That's the part the next shipment is paying for. Take your cut.

wtv_wolves.description:
Corvin Ashe. I walk the Vale's edge for the Deathguard, which means I'm the line between whatever is in those trees and the road up to Brill. I'm in Deathknell for supplies and for help, and you look like help.

The Bleak Worgs are getting bold. A year ago they kept to the deep Vale and you'd hear them and that was all. Now they come to the treeline at dusk and stand there, looking up the road, working out the slope.

That's what worries me. Not the hunger - the measuring. Thin the pack while the road is still too much trouble for them. Aim for the grey ones; the grey ones are the ones doing the thinking.
wtv_wolves.accept_text: They hunt at dusk. Aim for the grey ones - they lead.
wtv_wolves.turn_in_text:
Grey ones among them? Good. That's a season's worth of learning gone out of that pack.

They'll breed it back. They always do. But not before the frost, and I'll take the winter.

wtv_crawlers.description:
When you get out to the Vale, mind where you put your feet. I mean it. Stand still a moment out there and listen to the loam.

Nightcrawlers. They burrow all through the near end of the Vale and they come up under whatever walks over them, which is a perfectly good way to live if you're a worm and an appalling one if you're a ranger.

I have lost two boots to them. I'd like it known that I have lost considerably more dignity than boots, because the losing of a boot in soft ground is not a quiet or graceful event. Clear the young ones out of the loam before they're big enough to take the leg that's in the boot.
wtv_crawlers.accept_text: Under the roots. You'll feel them before you see them - get them before they grow.
wtv_crawlers.turn_in_text:
Good. I shall walk this stretch without doing the little hop I have been doing.

Don't tell the Brill garrison about the hop.

wtv_needler.description:
There's a duskbat above the Vale road that the locals have named, and things only get named around here when killing them has become a topic.

Ressan the Needler. Big old brute, teeth like his name, and he comes in low along the road at head height - which, for a bat, is a decision rather than an accident. He's got a flock that moves when he moves. I've watched him put three travellers on the ground in a month and he didn't feed on one of them.

Clear the flock off him first or they'll peel you while you're busy. Then put the Needler down. I'll be back at the treeline by the time you're there. With my boots on.
wtv_needler.accept_text: He nests above the road, flies low, and screams. Clear his flock first, then him.
wtv_needler.turn_in_text:
I heard it stop. Whole Vale heard it stop.

Road's walkable at dusk again. That's the first sentence of that kind I've been able to say this year.

wt_manor_reapers.description:
Watcher Pell. I've kept the Cold Hearth gate for a year, and they've called me back to Brill to tell them what I've seen there. In that year the reapers haven't stopped once.

They come up out of the manor cellars with scythes. Not shambling - working. They come up in a line, they spread along the hedge, and they cut, and there has been nothing growing in that garden to cut since before I was posted there. Then they go back down. Then they come up again.

I've stopped asking what they think they're harvesting. Clear the ones at the door, and mind the blades - those have been kept sharp by somebody, and it isn't the gardener.
wt_manor_reapers.accept_text: Up from the cellars, along the hedge. Be careful with the scythes.
wt_manor_reapers.turn_in_text:
Quiet at the hedge. That's an hour of quiet, maybe two.

You'll think me grim for saying it, but an hour is a great deal when you've had none.

wt_manor_dead.description:
Now that you've seen the hedge, look past it at the grounds, because the reapers aren't the half of it.

Zombies come in off the glades and the rotted ones come up through the lawn, and they all go the same way: toward the hall. Not toward me. Not toward the road. Toward the house, every time, as if the place were calling the staff in.

I've a horrible suspicion it is. Clear the gardens for me. I want to see how fast they fill up again, because the answer tells me what I'm actually guarding.
wt_manor_dead.accept_text: Clear the gardens - the zombies and the rotted ones both.
wt_manor_dead.turn_in_text:
Empty. For now.

I'll time it. If it's hours, the manor's drawing them. If it's days, it's just the glades. I'd rather know which before I have to write it in a report somebody acts on.

wt_aldous.description:
Right. The hall itself, and the thing at the hearth in it.

Reaper-Lord Aldous. Taller than the rest, scythe for an arm these days, and the others answer to him - I've watched the line along the hedge dress itself when he came to the door. He thinks the manor is his and he thinks the staff are still his, and in the most literal sense available he's correct, which is the problem.

His reapers will put themselves between you and him. They always do. Take them off him first, and then take the hall back, and then I will have guarded this gate for a year and have something to show for it.
wt_aldous.accept_text: Inside the hall, at the hearth. His reapers will guard him - take them first.
wt_aldous.turn_in_text:
[Pell looks at the manor door for a while before he answers.]

A year. I stood at that gate a year.

I'll go back out to the gate a while longer. The cellars want watching yet. But the hall is a house now instead of a household, and I'll take that.

wts_puddlejumpers.description:
Don't laugh. I can see you building up to it and I'd ask you to hold it in until I've finished.

Quillon, fisher, Whispering Shore. The Vile Fins have my boat. They have also got my nets, which they are wearing. On their heads. The small ones patrol the strand in my nets like a procession of the very worst magistrates you have ever seen.

Here's the thing, and this is why it isn't funny: the strand is how this village eats. While they hold it we don't fish, and the inn starts asking the Apothecary what's edible, and you do not want to be downwind of the answer. Clear the little ones off the sand.
wts_puddlejumpers.accept_text: Along the strand to the north-west. The little ones. Bring back my dignity if you find it.
wts_puddlejumpers.turn_in_text:
Sand's clear. I can get a line out tomorrow.

And no, you may not have a net back as a souvenir. Those are going back on a pole where they belong.

wts_pearls.description:
The little ones were the front rank. The ones at the back, the ones that stand still and make the noise - those are the oracles, and they're the reason any of this is organised.

They wear pearls. Salt-pearls, strung at the throat, and they use them to talk to the tide. I know how that sounds. I have fished this shore for thirty years and I am telling you the tide answers them, and that for the last few months what it's been saying has been wrong - wrong hours, wrong height, a slack water that turns when it shouldn't.

Take the pearls off them. Either I'm an old fool and nothing changes, or I'm right and the water goes back to keeping time.
wts_pearls.accept_text: The minor oracles carry them. And if the tide screams, run.
wts_pearls.turn_in_text:
[He turns one over, holding it up against the light off the water.]

Tide turned at the right hour this morning. First time since the spring.

I'd rather have been the old fool, if I'm honest. An old fool's shore is a safer place to work.

wts_gillrot.description:
Old Gillrot. He's the one with my boat.

He sits up on the big rock at the north end with a staff he's made out of a mast, and I know whose mast it was, and so does everyone who drinks in Brill. The other oracles keep him standing - I've seen him take a harpoon and I've seen them put him back together, so if you go at him straight you'll be there till the tide comes in.

Thin the oracles first. Then Gillrot. And listen - I want the boat, but I'll be straight with you, I want the mast more. A man ought to be buried with his own ship, not have it waved about by a murloc.
wts_gillrot.accept_text: He sits on the biggest rock. His oracles heal him - thin them first, then Gillrot.
wts_gillrot.turn_in_text:
That's Harl's mast. Twenty years he had that boat and he went down with it in a squall, and his widow is still in Brill, and she has had to look at that rock every day since.

I'll take it to her this evening. The boat can wait. Thank you, truly.

wto_converts.description:
Down. Behind the thorns, and don't look over the top of them - look through.

Dessa Vane, scouting for the Deathguard. That's the Crusader Outpost, and those are this week's converts. New ones come up that road every week, and they arrive wide-eyed and badly armed and absolutely certain, and that last part is what makes them dangerous rather than sad.

I know what you're about to feel when you get close enough to see their faces. Feel it afterwards. A convert who's been here a month is an Initiate, and an Initiate marches on Brill. Thin them while they're still the easier problem.
wto_converts.accept_text: They're green and enthusiastic. That makes them dangerous. Keep to the shadows.
wto_converts.turn_in_text:
Clean work, and you didn't start a general alarm, which is more than the last pair managed.

They'll send more. That's rather the point of a crusade. But not this week's column.

wto_initiates.description:
Now the rank behind them, and I'll be plain: this part is harder and you should treat it that way.

Initiates. Trained, properly armed, and devout in the settled way rather than the shouting way. They carry the banners, they hold the outpost's shape, and when the Crusade decides Brill is a problem worth solving, these are the ones who will be told to solve it.

Don't take more than two at once. I'm not being careful with your feelings - I've watched a Deathguard try three and I had to go back at dusk for what was left of him.
wto_initiates.accept_text: Better than the converts. Don't engage more than two at once.
wto_initiates.turn_in_text:
The banners are down. Good.

That outpost's shape comes from those men. Without them it's a camp of frightened recruits with a view of our road, and a frightened recruit is a much slower thing to worry about.

wto_korgal.description:
And there he is. Centre of the camp, under the standard. Meven Korgal.

He's a veteran. He was a veteran before he was a zealot, which is the dangerous order to do it in - he can hold a line, he can site a camp, and he prays like a man reading a map. Everything in that outpost that works, works because he's standing in it.

His recruits will rally to him; they adore him, and you'll have to go through that first. But I've watched this camp for a season and I'll tell you what I've concluded: take Korgal and the rest is tents.
wto_korgal.accept_text: He's at the heart of the camp, under the standard. His recruits will rally.
wto_korgal.turn_in_text:
[Dessa watches the camp through the thorns for a long moment.]

They're arguing. Three of them, by the standard, and nobody's stopped it.

That's it, then. That's an outpost becoming a crowd. I'll have my report up to Brill by dark.

wtf_farmhands.description:
Sit a moment and let me say this properly, because the Deathguard sent a lad last month who didn't let me finish and I've felt poorly about it since.

I'm Marren. Solliden was my husband's farm, and the dead out in its fields are his hands. I've taken a room in Brill. I couldn't sleep with them in the yard. They stayed on after he died, which was good of them. Then they stayed on after they died, which is the part nobody prepared any of us for.

They still work it. All hours, rusted tools, no crop and no direction, up and down rows that haven't held anything in years. They're not dangerous. They're just not stopping, and I can't watch it from this window any longer.

Go gently. They were good men and they worked hard for a man who didn't always deserve it.
wtf_farmhands.accept_text: Out in the fields. Put them down gently. They were good men.
wtf_farmhands.turn_in_text:
[She is quiet a while.]

Thank you. I'll see them buried at the top of the north field - it's the only part he never managed to drain, so nothing will ever be planted over them.

They'd have appreciated that. It was their favourite complaint.

wtf_threshers.description:
The other thing in my fields isn't dead. That's what I can't get anyone in Brill to understand.

The grain threshers still run. Nobody feeds them, nobody winds them, nobody has touched one since my husband was upright, and they go up and down those rows at all hours taking in whatever's in front of them. The blight got into the works somewhere and now they don't stop at the headland the way they're built to. They just turn and come back.

They've had the last of the harvest. There's nothing out there now but stubble and each other, and a machine that's run out of crop starts looking at the fence. Break them. I'd rather lose the iron than find out what they settle on next.
wtf_threshers.accept_text: Out in the rows at Solliden Farmstead. They don't stop at the headland any more.
wtf_threshers.turn_in_text:
Quiet out there. Properly quiet - I'd forgotten the fields had a sound of their own under all that clattering.

Take the scrap money. I've no use for iron and less for the memory of it.

wtf_goodman.description:
[She does not look up from the window.]

He's out by the far hedge. You'll know him - he's the only one out there carrying a pitchfork instead of a hoe, and he's the only one smiling.

My husband. Goodman Solliden. He worked that ground for thirty years and he was hard on the hands and harder on himself, and whatever is walking it now has his face and his stride and his grin, and the grin is wrong. It's the wrongness of it that I can't carry any more. Not the grief. The grin.

Some of the hands keep to him. You'll have to take them off him first. Then let him lie down.

I'll walk home and sit at my own window while you do it. I won't watch. But I'd like to be there.
wtf_goodman.accept_text: By the far hedge at Solliden Farmstead. The one with the pitchfork. Some of the hands keep to him.
wtf_goodman.turn_in_text:
[A long silence.]

The field's empty.

Thank you. I'll have him in beside the hands at the top of the north field, and that's the whole family seen to, and I can shut this window at last.

wtp_lurkers.description:
Don't come past the stones. Not a warning, just - there's silt there and it's deeper than it looks and I'd have to come and get you.

Oswin. I live at Stillwater because nobody else wants to, which suits me, and I'd ask you not to improve on that arrangement.

The lurkers in the silt are the neighbours. Crab-looking things, mostly harmless, and I'd got to where I could walk the margin without bother. That's finished. Something's put them up - they come at the ankles now, in numbers, and they've stopped minding the lamp. I can't fish the margin and I can't cross it, which between them is most of what I do.

Thin them. I'd rather they stayed, mind. Just fewer, and politer.
wtp_lurkers.accept_text: In the silt along the margin. Watch your ankles.
wtp_lurkers.turn_in_text:
I walked the whole margin this morning. Both ways.

There's still some out in the deep silt, and good. A pond with nothing in it is just a hole full of water.

wtp_dead.description:
Now, the other lot, and I'll want you to hear me out because it sounds daft said plainly.

The Rotting Dead come up out of Stillwater. Not the bank - the water, straight up out of it, at all hours, and they sing. Same tune every time. It's a hymn, I'm fairly sure, and I was a churchgoing man a long time ago, and I cannot place it and it is driving me to distraction.

I've tried asking them. I've tried singing it back. The second one was a mistake and we'll leave it there.

I came out here for the quiet. Give me the quiet back.
wtp_dead.accept_text: Out of the pond, at all hours. They sing. You'll hear it before you see them.
wtp_dead.turn_in_text:
[He listens.]

Nothing but the water.

I'll tell you the strange part - I've been trying to place that tune for two years and now it's gone I expect I never will. Can't say I mind. There's some things it's better to have stopped than solved.

wtp_murk.description:
Right. The last of it, and the reason I asked about the others first.

There's something at the bottom of my pond. I call it Murk. I've never had a proper look at it and I don't intend to - what I know is what the water does. It bloats. Every drowned thing that goes in, it takes, and it swells, and then it brings them up again on my shore. Not whole. Arranged.

That's where the lurkers have been getting their nerve from, I reckon. Whatever's feeding them, it's down there, and it's grown.

Take the lurkers off the margin first, because they'll come when it moves. Then go in after it. And Oswin's advice, free: don't let it get behind you in the deep silt.
wtp_murk.accept_text: At the bottom of the pond. The lurkers will come when it moves - take them first.
wtp_murk.turn_in_text:
[He is standing at the water's edge when you come back, which he never does.]

It's gone down flat. Whole surface. I can see the stones on the bottom for the first time since I came here.

I'm going to sit out here a while. You go on.

wta_servants.description:
Envoy Sorren, speaking for Brill. I've just come back from the Agamand mill, so you'll excuse me if I keep this brief.

That mill belonged to the Agamands. The staff are still in it. Not the family - the SERVANTS, the ones who cooked and swept and carried, and they are still cooking and sweeping and carrying in a house with no one left to do it for.

Brill needs the grain stores. That is the entire substance of my posting. And the moment anyone goes near the stores, those servants stop being tragic and start being murderers, because somebody once told them the grain was the family's and nobody has ever told them otherwise.

Clear the ones at the stores. I take no pleasure in it and I'd thank you not to describe it to me afterwards.
wta_servants.accept_text: At the grain stores in Agamand Mills, north of Brill. They'll be peaceable until you touch it. Then they won't.
wta_servants.turn_in_text:
The stores are ours. I'll have carts up from Brill within the week.

I have written 'the household was dispersed' in my report. It is a coward's sentence and I am going to leave it in.

wta_keys.description:
There's something under the mill I have not put in a report yet.

The cellars are holding farmers. Living ones, taken off the Solliden road and the western plots, shackled to the posts in the cellar and left. Not eaten. Not turned. Left - the way you leave a thing you have been told to keep and have not been told what for.

The servants carry the keys on them. They won't give them up and they won't use them. They just carry them, the way they carry everything else in that house: because it is theirs to carry.

Get me the keys. Whatever else we are, we are not going to be the people who knew about that cellar and did the paperwork instead.
wta_keys.accept_text: Up at Agamand Mills, north of here. The servants carry the keys. They won't use them, they just carry them.
wta_keys.turn_in_text:
Every post unlocked. Good.

Some of them wouldn't come up. Three years in the dark will do that, and I'm not going to drag a man into Brill to be grateful at him. We'll leave food at the stair and the door open and let them decide.

It's more choice than the Agamands gave them.

wta_thurman.description:
The mill-house itself, then. And the miller in it.

Thurman Agamand. He was the miller before he was the lord, which the family never liked mentioned - the lordship came late and came by plague, when everybody above him in the line stopped being available. He's in the house now with what's left of them, and they are very much a family still: they eat together, they sit in the right chairs, they keep to the rooms they always kept to.

I have stood at that door and listened to a dead man ask a dead woman to pass something. I'd like that house back and I would like to stop hearing it.

The family will come at you together. They always do. That's rather the point of them.
wta_thurman.accept_text: In the mill-house at Agamand Mills, with the family. They'll come at you together.
wta_thurman.turn_in_text:
It's a building again. That's all I wanted it to be.

Brill gets its grain, the cellars are open, and the Agamands are finally as finished as everyone has been pretending they were for years. I'll sleep properly tonight, for the first time in a month.

wtc_wights.description:
Keeper Halvard. The Agamand crypt gate is mine, and I haven't been through it in a long time, and I'd like to stop having to say that sentence.

The crypt is Agamand ground - vaults, name-stones, the whole dynasty laid out in order down there. My post is to keep it. Then the wights woke up in it, and a man with one lantern and a ring of keys does not clear a vault full of wights, so my post became standing at a door being very reliable about it, until they sent me here to ask for help.

They hold the vaults now. They've been moving things - I can hear stone going over stone at night, and I have a horrible idea they are tidying.

Go down and clear them out. I'll hold the gate. I'm very good at the gate.
wtc_wights.accept_text: The Agamand Family Crypt, north of here. Down past the gate, in the vaults. I'll get back to the door and hold it.
wtc_wights.turn_in_text:
Quiet down there? Good. I can hear the lantern hissing, and that's all.

I'll go down myself tomorrow and see what they moved. Tomorrow, mind. A man should be allowed one more night of being good at the gate.

wtc_dargol.description:
There's one more down there and he isn't like the others.

Captain Dargol commanded the Agamand guard. The wights wander; Dargol PATROLS. Same route, same turns, same pauses at the same vault mouths, and he has been walking it for years to protect a family that is dust in boxes behind him.

I'll be honest with you, because it has been bothering me and there's nobody at that gate to say it to: I don't think he's wrong, exactly. He was given a thing to keep and he is keeping it. I've a great deal of sympathy for that, standing where I've stood.

It doesn't change what needs doing. He'll have wights with him - he always does. Take them, then him, and do it cleanly.
wtc_dargol.accept_text: The lower vaults of the Agamand Family Crypt. He patrols with an escort. Take the escort first.
wtc_dargol.turn_in_text:
[Halvard is quiet for a moment.]

Then the vaults are kept by me again, which is how it's written, and I'm going to try to feel like that's an improvement.

Give me a day. I'll get there.

wth_mongrels.description:
Warden Brask. I hold the line at Garren's Haunt, and I'm in Brill for one night to find people who'll be useful out there.

The Rot Hides keep mongrels. Not pets - stock. They run them loose through the old fields ahead of the pack to turn up anything worth digging, and the fields have been a kennel for about two seasons now. You can smell it from the line when the wind's wrong.

The gnolls are the problem, I know that, and we'll get to the gnolls. But I'm not walking anyone into that camp with a hundred mongrels loose behind us. Clear the fields first. Front door before the house.
wth_mongrels.accept_text: Loose in the old fields, ahead of the camp. Front door before the house.
wth_mongrels.turn_in_text:
Fields are walkable. That's the approach open.

Now we can talk about the camp like people with options instead of people with a plan.

wth_gnolls.description:
Now the camp, and I want you going in knowing what these are, because 'gnoll' makes people picture something stupid.

Rot Hides. Stitched hide, clubs about the length of your arm, and they dig. That's their whole industry out there - they open graves, they take what's in them, and they take their time about it. There's a pit at the back of that camp that I've been told about and have decided not to look at.

They're not stupid. They're organised, and they've been left alone long enough to get comfortable, and comfortable is the thing I'm actually out there to spoil. Get in among them.
wth_gnolls.accept_text: Garren's Haunt, north of Brill, in the camp proper. They're organised, so don't let them get comfortable.
wth_gnolls.turn_in_text:
Good. They'll be moving the pit tonight, which means they're reacting to us instead of the other way about.

That's the first time that's been true since I took this line.

wth_maggot.description:
Last piece. The one they follow.

Maggot Eye. Scarred to pieces, rotted halfway through, and bigger than anything else in that camp - and before you ask, no, the rot doesn't slow him. I've watched him take a crossbow bolt through the shoulder and finish what he was doing first.

He leads for the simplest reason there is: he bites harder than they do, and every one of them has found that out personally. Which means it works the other way too. Take him in front of them and that camp doesn't appoint a successor, it scatters.

He'll have his own close to him. Clear those, then finish it.
wth_maggot.accept_text: Centre of the camp. He'll have his own close by - clear them first.
wth_maggot.turn_in_text:
[Brask watches the smoke over the fields.]

They're going east. Not regrouping - going. Carrying what they can and leaving the pit.

I've held this line for a year and a half. I'd quite like to go and stand somewhere else for a bit.

etl_dusk.description:
Deathguard Linnea. I keep order at the Landing, which on paper is a serious posting and in practice is largely bats.

They roost in the mooring ropes. All day, upside down, perfectly content - and then a zeppelin comes in, the ropes go taut, and the entire roost drops on whoever is standing under them with their luggage.

I have had two passengers refuse to disembark. I have had a goblin quote me a surcharge. The tower only works if people are willing to stand beneath it, and at present they are not. Clear the ropes.
etl_dusk.accept_text: In the mooring ropes above the platform. They drop when the lines go taut.
etl_dusk.turn_in_text:
Ropes are clear and the midday arrival got off without anyone screaming.

It isn't glorious work. It's the work. The Dark Lady's shipping line does not care whether I find it dignified.

etl_dead.description:
Next problem, and this one is costing real money.

The road between Brill and the Landing is full of wandering zombies. They don't attack the carts. They don't rob them. They stand in the road, and when a carter shouts at them they look at him, and then they carry on standing in the road.

A cart that can't get through is a cart that doesn't come back, and we are three years into convincing the living trade routes that a Forsaken port is worth the detour. I will not lose that to a crowd that cannot be reasoned with and cannot be insulted. Clear the road.
etl_dead.accept_text: Along the Brill road. They won't move for shouting. They won't move for anything.
etl_dead.turn_in_text:
Carts are running. The afternoon run came through without stopping once.

Write that down somewhere, would you. Somebody in the Undercity thinks this post guards itself.

etl_remnants.description:
South of here is the thing this posting is actually about, whatever the duty roster says about bats.

The Ruins of Lordaeron. The old capital, the gate down to the Undercity, and the remnants - what's left of the men who were in it when it fell. They don't leave. They can't, as far as anyone has worked out. They walk the approach and they snap at whoever passes, and what makes it hard is that some of them are still in formation.

I've been told to keep the approach passable and I've been told not to make a ceremony of it. So I won't. Clear the approach, and if any of them are wearing Menethil colours, don't tell me about it.
etl_remnants.accept_text: South of the Landing, on the approach road. Keep it passable.
etl_remnants.turn_in_text:
Approach is clear.

They'll be back. They're always back - something about that ground puts them on their feet again, and nobody above me is interested in finding out what.

That's a question for people with better titles than mine.

etl_signets.description:
One more thing from the approach, and this one isn't on any roster.

The remnants wear signet rings. Court signets - the old Lordaeron houses, the ones that had business in that building when it fell. Most of them are worthless metal with a crest on, and I want them anyway.

Some of those houses have people left. Living ones, scattered west and south, who have spent years not knowing whether their father died in the throne room or walked out of it. A ring with a crest and a place it was found is not much of an answer, but it is one, and nobody else is collecting them because nobody else thinks it's worth the trouble.

Bring me what you find. I'll do the rest of it myself.
etl_signets.accept_text: Off the remnants on the approach. Court signets - you'll know the crests.
etl_signets.turn_in_text:
[She lays them out in a row on the rail and does not pick any of them up.]

Two of these I recognise. One I've been hoping not to see for a long while.

Thank you. I'll write the letters tonight. It's the only part of this posting I'd call worth doing.

etm_restless.description:
If you go up to Faol's Rest, mind the rows. The soil's loose and it's loose for a reason.

Morvyn, gravekeeper of Faol's Rest. I've walked down to Brill because I can't keep it alone any more. It's pilgrims' ground, most of them, people who walked a long way to be buried near a good man and got their wish about a week before the plague made it meaningless.

They won't stay down. They come up through the rows and then they STAND there, in the lines, between the stones, facing the same way they were laid. Not wandering. Standing, in formation, in a graveyard. I've kept ground for a long time and I have never seen anything behave like that.

Put them back. And be careful of the rows while you do it - I'd rather not have to re-dig what I've already dug.
etm_restless.accept_text: Up through the rows, standing between the stones. Mind the soil.
etm_restless.turn_in_text:
Rows are empty. I've tamped them back down.

They'll rise again - something up there keeps lifting them and I haven't found it. But they'll rise into tidy ground, and that's the part I can control.

etm_seals.description:
Now I'll tell you why they keep getting up, because I think I've worked it out and I don't like it.

Faol's own grave is sealed. Not a slab - a ring of carved stone set into the ground around it, and the carving is the seal, and the ring is what keeps the whole yard quiet. It's been there since the pilgrims were.

The restless have been taking the fragments. Lifting them out and carrying them off into the rows, one at a time, and every one that goes makes the next night worse. I can't tell whether they're being driven to it or whether they just want it gone.

Get the fragments back to me. If that ring fails completely I don't think I'll be writing anybody a report about it.
etm_seals.accept_text: Faol's Rest, north-east of Brill. The restless carry the fragments off into the rows. Bring back what you find.
etm_seals.turn_in_text:
[He fits each one back into the ring by hand, turning it until it sits.]

That's the circuit closed. You can feel the difference in the ground - go on, stand there a moment.

Quieter. That's all I want out of a graveyard.

etm_melrache.description:
And then there's the living problem, which is somehow the one that offends me most.

There's a Scarlet captain camped in my yard. Melrache. He's got men digging - opening graves, going through them, and calling it a crusade because the word makes a shovel into a sacrament.

I want to be clear about my objection. It isn't that he's Scarlet. It's that these are PILGRIMS. They walked all that way. They chose this ground. Whatever they thought they were doing with their lives, they finished it by coming to lie near a man they believed was good, and that officer is pulling them out of the earth in handfuls to see if they're carrying anything.

Some of the restless will be up when you go in - they always are when he's digging. Then have a word with the captain.
etm_melrache.accept_text: He's camped in the yard at Faol's Rest with men digging. The restless will be up around him.
etm_melrache.turn_in_text:
Shovels down. Good.

I'll fill in what he opened myself. Slowly, and properly, with the right stone back over each one. It'll take me the better part of a month.

I'm looking forward to it, if I'm honest.

etg_wretches.description:
Gunther Lorn. I watch Brightwater Lake, which sounds like a soft posting and isn't. They've called me down to the Undercity to report on it, and you're the first one who's listened.

The Drowned Wretches come out of Brightwater at dusk. Up the shingle, onto the bank, and they moan - and here's the part the duty roster leaves out, because I've tried to put it in twice: they moan NAMES. Not words. Names of people the lake took, and some of them I know, because I was posted there when it took them.

I am not a superstitious man and I do not want to discuss what that means. I want them back in the water and I want to do my shift without being read a list.
etg_wretches.accept_text: They come up the shingle at dusk. Put them back in the water.
etg_wretches.turn_in_text:
Quiet bank tonight.

I'll not pretend that's permanent. But I got through a shift without hearing my sergeant's name, and I'll take the night.

etg_ice.description:
Something else about that water, and you can test this yourself while you're out there.

It's cold. Wrong cold - colder than the air above it, in every season, and it has been since before I took the post. Lake water doesn't do that.

The shades along the shore hoard shards of black ice. They carry them about, they don't use them for anything, and wherever a shade has been standing a while the ground is hard. I've a theory that the shards are the cause rather than the symptom, and I'd like to be proved right or wrong before another winter.

Strip the shards off them and bring them back to me. If I'm wrong I'll say so.
etg_ice.accept_text: The shades along the shore of Brightwater Lake hoard them. Bring back what they're carrying.
etg_ice.turn_in_text:
Still freezing. Hours out of the water and the bucket's rimed up.

So I'm half right - they're not the only cause, but they're not innocent either. That's more than I knew yesterday, and the shore was walkable this morning for the first time since autumn.

etg_bethor.description:
Right. Now the middle of the lake, and the reason none of the rest of it has worked.

Bethor Iceshard. He's a shade, or he was - he's got too cold to finish dying, which is not a thing I can explain to you any better than that. He stands out there at the centre and he pulls the warmth out of whatever comes near. Birds go down over that water. I've seen it.

The weeping ones keep close to him, and they'll come for you first; they always do. Take them off him, then put him out.

And listen - don't stand still out there. Whatever he does, he does it to things that stop moving.
etg_bethor.accept_text: The centre of Brightwater Lake. The weeping ones keep close to him. Don't stand still.
etg_bethor.turn_in_text:
[Lorn has his hand flat on the surface of the water.]

Cold. Just - cold. Lake cold.

That's the first ordinary thing this water has done since I was posted there. I'm going to go and write a report that nobody will understand the significance of.

eth_converts.description:
Hallam, scouting. Down a bit - that's it.

That's the Crusader's Outpost, and that lot by the fire are this season's recruits. Listen to them for a minute. Go on.

Loud, aren't they. Young, loud, and about as prepared for a fight as a sack of apples - and I want you to hold onto that impression for exactly as long as it takes to remember they came here on purpose, to a place everyone told them was full of us, because a man in a tabard told them it would mean something.

A month of drill and they're Initiates. Then they're a column, and the column comes up our road. Do it now, while it's still the easier job.
eth_converts.accept_text: By the fire at the outpost. Do it now, while it's the easier job.
eth_converts.turn_in_text:
Clean. And you went in and came out without the whole camp standing to, which is the bit I actually care about.

More will come up that road. There's always more. But that's this season's column that won't be walking it.

eth_initiates.description:
Now the gate itself, and the men on it are a different proposition.

Initiates. They've been drilled, they're properly armed, and they've got past the shouting stage into the quiet kind of certainty, which is worse. They hold the gate, they hold the watch rotation, and they hold whatever it is that outpost doesn't want seen - there's a tent at the back that nobody but Initiates goes into, and I've been watching for a season.

I'd dearly love to know what's in it. Failing that, I'd settle for the gate being thin enough that somebody can go and look.
eth_initiates.accept_text: On the gate and the watch rotation. They're drilled - treat them like it.
eth_initiates.turn_in_text:
Gate's thin. I had a clear look at the back of the camp for the first time.

The tent's a map table. Just a map table, with our road on it, and a lot of marks around Brill.

I'd have preferred something sinister. Sinister is usually slower.

eth_brennic.description:
Crusader Brennic. Commands the outpost, and he's the reason it works.

I'll give him this much: he's good. He's strong, he keeps his men fed, and he's merciless in the specific way that doesn't come from temper - he's never once lost control up there, which makes him much harder to fight and much harder to wait out.

His recruits will throw themselves at you for him, and they'll mean it. Get through them and finish it with Brennic himself. That garrison is one man's discipline in the shape of a camp, and when he goes it will go with him.
eth_brennic.accept_text: He commands from the centre. His recruits will rally to him first.
eth_brennic.turn_in_text:
[Hallam watches through the thorns a long time before she lowers the glass.]

They've struck the map tent. No orders given that I saw - somebody just started doing it and the rest joined in.

That's a garrison turning back into people. The road's ours for a season at least. Good work.

etr_skitterers.description:
When you go into the Vale, don't wander. The webbing starts a few paces in and you won't see it until you're in it.

Ravel. I hunt the Vale, which at the moment means I hunt spiders, because there isn't room in there for anything else any more. I'm in the Undercity to sell venom and find help, in that order.

The skitterers breed faster than I can work. I clear a stretch, I come back in a fortnight, and it's thicker than when I started. And their bite doesn't kill - it stops you. That's the part that keeps me careful. Nothing in Venomweb has to hurt you; it only has to make you stand still for a while.

Thin them with me. I've been doing this alone for a long time.
etr_skitterers.accept_text: Venomweb Vale, through the webbing and deeper in. Their bite stops you, so keep moving.
etr_skitterers.turn_in_text:
That's a proper dent. I've not had one of those in months.

I'll take the east stretch tomorrow while it's thin. Don't look so pleased - we're still losing. Just slower.

etr_sacs.description:
While you're in there, there's a thing worth cutting out of them.

Venom sacs. The Apothecaries in the Undercity pay a frankly indecent amount for Venomweb venom - it does something to a plague draught that nothing else does, and they've stopped pretending they can get it anywhere else.

So: some for the Undercity, because the coin keeps me in bolts and I'd rather not starve in a wood full of spiders. Some for the war, because they'll have it off me either way and it's better to be the one selling.

And some for me. You can want a reason for that one. You're not getting it.
etr_sacs.accept_text: Cut them out of the skitterers in Venomweb Vale. Careful with the sacs. They're thin.
etr_sacs.turn_in_text:
Good clean cuts, no spoilage. You've done this before.

The Undercity gets its share, the war gets its share. Mine goes in the box and the box is my business.

etr_mother.description:
Now the one that matters. Every spider in that Vale came out of her.

Mother Venomweb. Venom-fat, old, and clever in a way I've stopped being comfortable about - she doesn't rush, she doesn't panic, and twice now she's moved her brood before I got to where they were. Something in there is doing arithmetic.

Her skitterers will come at you in a wave when she feels you coming, so break those first or you'll be stood still when she arrives, and standing still is the whole trick of that wood.

I've been working up to this for two years. I'd rather not do it alone.
etr_mother.accept_text: Deep in Venomweb Vale. Her brood comes first. Break them, then her.
etr_mother.turn_in_text:
[Ravel sits down on a root, which you have not seen her do.]

Two years.

The Vale will fill up again. Something always does. But it'll be a wood with spiders in it instead of a spider with a wood around it, and I can hunt a wood.

Take the venom. All of it. I'm done counting it out.

etb_worgs.description:
You're the one Joss sent? Then you've seen the state of Balnir.

Edric. Stablehand - still, apparently, though there's been nothing to hand in the stable for years. I keep what's left of Balnir standing because somebody ought to, and I've come into Brill because I can't do the rest alone.

The Bleak Worgs have the paddock. They've denned in it, and anything that wanders in through the broken rail doesn't wander back out. It's a good paddock. Good posts, good drainage, my master's father laid that fence and it's still square.

I'd like it to be a paddock again and not a larder. Clear them out of it.
etb_worgs.accept_text: In the paddock, through the broken rail. They've denned in it.
etb_worgs.turn_in_text:
I'll get the rail back up this afternoon. It's a two-man job and I'll do it in four hours instead of two, which is fine, because it's my afternoon.

Thank you. It looks like a farm again from the road.

etb_stableboys.description:
Now the hard half, and I'd ask you to let me finish before you go out.

The stableboys are still there. They never left - not when the plague came through, not after. They're out in the paddock with pitchforks doing the evening round, and they've been doing the evening round for years, and the horses have been gone for every one of them.

I knew them. I was one of them, in the sense that mattered - I just happened to be in the far field on the wrong week and came out of it differently.

They're waiting for a master who isn't coming and horses that aren't there. Let them stop. Go gently, and don't take the forks off them. They were proud of those.
etb_stableboys.accept_text: Out in the paddock on the evening round. Go gently. Leave them their forks.
etb_stableboys.turn_in_text:
[He is a long time answering.]

That's the round finished. First time it's been finished since I came back.

I'll bury them along the rail where they used to sit and argue about nothing. Then I'll do the evening round myself, properly, the once, and then I'll stop too.

etb_vachon.description:
There's somebody else out there, and he was never a stablehand.

Captain Vachon led the Balnir militia - farm lads with billhooks, mostly, and him with an actual commission from an actual lord, and he drilled them in the Balnir yard every week like it was a proper garrison. We laughed about it. He knew we laughed about it and he drilled us anyway.

He's still holding the farm. That's what he's doing out there, and he's doing it well, which is the trouble. He's got the dead organised in a way they are not organised anywhere else in this valley.

His lads will stand with him. Of course they will. He was the only one who ever treated them like soldiers.
etb_vachon.accept_text: Holding the yard with what's left of the militia. They'll stand with him.
etb_vachon.turn_in_text:
[Edric looks out over the empty yard for a while.]

He held it longer than anyone had any right to ask. Three years after there was nothing left to hold.

I'll put him at the gate end, facing the road. He'd have wanted the view of the approach, and I'd like somebody out there still watching it, even if it's only in the arrangement of the stones.

etd_acolytes.description:
Warden Ysolde Grave. When you go up to the Cult's farm, keep the barn between you and the farmhouse.

The Cult of the Damned has the farm. Not raiders, not a warband - a congregation, and they work it like a farm, which is the part that unsettles people who go up there expecting something theatrical.

The acolytes are the ones doing the calling. They stand in the yard at the hours they've been told to stand in it and they reach for things that ought not to be reachable, and every time they do it the ground up there gets a little worse. The Undercity wants them silent. I want them silent for reasons that are mine.

Start in the yard. They don't post a watch - they genuinely do not expect to be interrupted.
etd_acolytes.accept_text: The Cult of the Damned Farm, in the yard at the calling hours. They don't post a watch.
etd_acolytes.turn_in_text:
Yard's clear and nothing answered them this evening.

That hill's had its first quiet dusk since I was posted there. Don't get comfortable - the cellar's still full.

etd_ledger.description:
They keep books. I want you to sit with that for a moment, because everybody's first reaction is to laugh and the laugh is wrong.

Names. Tallies. Debts - who owes what, and to whom, and what's been accepted as payment. A cult that keeps a ledger is not a mob of lunatics, it's an INSTITUTION, and an institution has a structure and a catchment and a list of people who have already said yes.

The pages are on the bodies. Each of them carries their own section, which tells you something about how little they trust one another.

Get me the pages. The Undercity will want the names, and I want to know how far down that hill the list goes.
etd_ledger.accept_text: The acolytes at the Cult of the Damned Farm each carry a section. They don't trust each other with the whole.
etd_ledger.turn_in_text:
[She reads with her jaw set.]

There are Brill names in this. Living and otherwise.

I'll not act on it tonight and I'll not hand it up until I've read every line. Half of being right about something like this is being slow about it.

etd_thaddeus.description:
The cellar, then. And the man issuing the orders from it.

Overseer Thaddeus. He hasn't come up into the yard once in the time I've watched this farm - he sits at the bottom and the instructions come up, and the acolytes carry them out to the hour. The fanatics stay close to him and they are a different animal from what you've fought in the yard: the acolytes believe, the fanatics have stopped needing to.

Take the fanatics off him first. Then finish it.

And when you're down there - look at how the cellar's dug. That's the thing I actually want to know about, and I'd rather you saw it with your own eyes before I put ideas in your head.
etd_thaddeus.accept_text: The deepest cellar under the farmhouse at the Cult of the Damned Farm. His fanatics stay close.
etd_thaddeus.turn_in_text:
You saw it, then. The dug part. The way it keeps going.

I know. I've been looking at the spoil heaps for a season trying to work out where all that earth came from and telling myself it was a root cellar.

There's a Boneward named Calder who needs to hear about this today.

ets_bowmen.description:
Hollowmere. I'm back from the north coast for a day, so let me tell you about the Watch Post while I've got you.

The Scarlet Watch Post sits above the north coast road, and their bowmen walk it. Not a patrol in the sense of looking for trouble. They walk it to shoot whatever comes along it, and they're good, and the road is the only flat way along this coast.

I've watched them take a carter. Not Forsaken - a carter, a living one, out of Brill on the Hillsbrad run, and they shot him off the seat and left the horse standing there for most of a day.

Get the bowmen off that road. Everything else up there is a conversation for afterwards.
ets_bowmen.accept_text: On the north coast road, below the Watch Post. They shoot anything that walks it.
ets_bowmen.turn_in_text:
Road's walkable. I watched a cart go the whole length of it this morning and nothing happened, which should not feel like news.

Stay low going back up the slope. The post has noticed.

ets_zealots.description:
The post itself now, and you'll hear it before you're in range of it.

Zealots. They preach while they fight - mid-swing, properly preaching, full sermon, and they do not stop when they're losing. I've taken one down a slope with an arrow in him and he was still going at the bottom.

I've listened to a great deal of it from this slope and I'll tell you what's in it, since you're going anyway: it's about cleansing, and it's about us, and it is extremely specific about Brill.

So it isn't just noise, and I'd rather it stopped being said out loud where recruits can hear it.
ets_zealots.accept_text: Inside the Scarlet Watch Post. They preach while they fight, and it doesn't stop them.
ets_zealots.turn_in_text:
Quieter up there.

I've been on this slope four months listening to what they intend to do to my town. You've no idea what an hour of nothing sounds like.

ets_preachers.description:
Now the ones at the back, and I want you taking these seriously because I didn't, once.

The preachers don't carry much. That's the mistake - you look at a man in robes behind two ranks of zealots and you make a judgement about which of them is the problem.

They call fire down. Not a torch, not a flask: FIRE, out of nothing, onto whoever they've decided is faithless, and they decide fast. I've got the scars under this sleeve from the day I learned to pick them out of a line first.

Pick them out of the line first. That's the whole of the advice and it's all I've got.
ets_preachers.accept_text: At the back of the Scarlet Watch Post, behind the zealots. Pick them out of the line first.
ets_preachers.turn_in_text:
Good. You can see the difference in how the post moves now - they're bunching, because nobody's covering them.

That's what those robes were worth. Everybody up there knew it except the people we keep sending up the slope.

ets_vishas.description:
And the cells. I've left this one until last on purpose and I'll not dress it up.

Interrogator Vishas runs the Watch Post's cells. He is patient, he is methodical, and he keeps proper hours - he stops for the evening, which is somehow the detail that has stayed with me.

There are people in there. Some of them living, taken off the coast road; some of them ours, which the Crusade considers a different category of question and asks differently. Nobody has come out of those cells, in either direction, in the four months I've been on this slope.

His zealots hold the stair. Go through them, and empty the cells, and do not leave that man upright behind you.
ets_vishas.accept_text: The cells under the Scarlet Watch Post. His zealots hold the stair.
ets_vishas.turn_in_text:
[Hollowmere does not ask about the cells for a while.]

How many came out walking?

...Good. That's more than I'd braced for. Get them down the slope before dark and I'll take the report to Brill myself - I want to be the one who says it out loud.

brl_dispatch.description:
You're going east, I hear. Then do something useful on the way.

This is for Gravekeeper Morvyn at Faol's Rest. Sealed, and it stays sealed, and I'll know.

I could send a messenger. I've sent four. One of them arrived, two came back having thought better of the hills, and the fourth is a subject I'd rather not open before noon. Morvyn's reports to me have been equally reliable in the other direction, which means the two of us have been running a graveyard and a garrison on either side of a gap neither of us can cross.

Put it in his hand. Not on a stone, not under a lantern. His hand.
brl_dispatch.accept_text: Over the hills east, to Gravekeeper Morvyn at Faol's Rest. In his hand.
brl_dispatch.turn_in_text:
[Morvyn breaks the seal with his thumb and reads it twice.]

He wants to know whether my ground is quiet. Rennick. Asking after my GROUND.

I'll write back. Tell him it's quiet, and tell him I said it in those words - he'll know what I mean by it, which is more than I can say for most people I've had to explain this yard to.

brl_guard_smelt.description:
Before you go anywhere - do you know what that building by the east market is? No. Nobody does.

It's a forge. Brill has a forge, brand new, paid for out of the Undercity, and it has been standing cold since the day they finished it because not one person in this town will admit they don't know how to light it.

I'm not having my kit fall apart while a perfectly good forge sits there being decorative. There's copper ore in these hills. Take it to the forge, smelt it into bars, and bring them to me so I can see with my own eyes that the thing works.

Then I'll tell you what they're for.
brl_guard_smelt.accept_text: Copper ore out of the Tirisfal hills, smelted at the Brill forge.
brl_guard_smelt.turn_in_text:
[He turns a bar over, twice.]

It works. The forge works.

Right. Now I'll tell you the rest of it, and you're going to need those bars back.

brl_guard_bracers.description:
Here's the rest of it, then.

Bars are a start. Bars aren't armour. What I want to know - what the garrison wants to know, though they'd rather I framed it as my idea - is whether anything that comes off that forge is worth WEARING.

So: bracers. Copper, at the Brill forge, made by you. Not bought, not found on something, not traded off a goblin at the Landing. Made.

If a stranger can walk in off the road and come out with a pair that hold together, then this town can arm itself, and we stop waiting on a cart from the Undercity every time somebody's strap goes.
brl_guard_bracers.accept_text: At the Brill forge, from your own bars. Made, not bought.
brl_guard_bracers.turn_in_text:
[He puts one on, flexes, puts the other on.]

These'll do. These'll more than do.

I'm going to walk past the barracks wearing them and say nothing, and I am going to enjoy the next hour enormously.

brl_locket.description:
The locket came off one of the wandering dead - the sort of thing you stop noticing you've picked up until it's in your hand at the end of a long walk.

It's tarnished almost black. The portrait inside has gone; there's a shape where a face was and nothing you could swear to. The inscription on the back has held up better than the rest of it, because it was cut deep by somebody who wanted it to last:

'For Marren, from Aldric.'

There is a Widow Marren at the Solliden Farmstead, west of Brill.
brl_locket.accept_text: Take it to the Widow Marren at the Solliden Farmstead, west of Brill.
brl_locket.turn_in_text:
[She does not take it straight away.]

Aldric was my husband's brother. He went east with the levy and we never heard, and my husband would never say the word 'dead' about him - he'd say 'not back yet', right up until he stopped saying anything at all.

So he was out there. All this time, out on the glades, not back yet.

Thank you. I'll put it with the two of them at the top of the north field. That's the whole family, now.

ets_bowman_orders.description:
Torn out of a bowman's quiver, stiff with what's dried on it.

It's a set of orders, and it is a good deal more organised than a watch post has any business being. Troop positions along the north coast. Patrol times, written out by the hour. And a map - a proper drawn map of the coast road, with the Brill approaches marked on it in a careful hand.

This isn't a garrison defending a hill. This is somebody planning a route.

Deathguard Rennick holds the Brill gate, and he will want to see this today rather than tomorrow.
ets_bowman_orders.accept_text: Take them to Deathguard Rennick at the Brill gate. Today.
ets_bowman_orders.turn_in_text:
[Rennick reads it standing up, which he does not normally bother to do.]

They've timed our patrols. Look - there, and there. That's my rotation, written in somebody else's hand.

I'm changing it tonight. And then I'm going to find out which of the carters on that road has been counting for them.

etd_ledger_courier.description:
I've bound the pages. Now I need somebody who can read them, and that isn't me and it isn't anyone in this city I'd trust with a list of Brill names.

Half this ledger is in a cipher. Not a good one - it's the kind of cipher you use when you're keeping secrets from your own congregation rather than from an enemy, which tells you plenty on its own.

The man I want is Keeper Oswin, at Raven Hill Cemetery in Silverpine, through the pass north-west of Brill. He kept records for the old church and he has a head for exactly this sort of thing, and he owes me.

Take the bundle. Don't read it on the road - not for secrecy. For your own evening.
etd_ledger_courier.accept_text: To Keeper Oswin at Raven Hill Cemetery, through the pass north-west into Silverpine.
etd_ledger_courier.turn_in_text:
[Oswin weighs the bundle without opening it.]

Ysolde Grave. There's a name I've not had to think about in a while.

She's right, I can read it. I can read half of it today and the rest when you've done me a service, because there's a reason the other half won't open and it isn't the cipher.

sp_ledger_cipher.description:
Here's the trouble, and it's not the hand it's written in.

The cult keyed the second half of this ledger to the Agamand family seals. Not as a code - as a LOCK. The marks only resolve against the real seals, and the only person who can match them is somebody who has stood in the Agamand mansion and seen them cut into the stone, which you have and I have not and am not about to.

So I can do this work, but I can't do it here, and I can't do it while the ground behind this cemetery is behaving the way it is.

The husks come up out of the back plots and they come to the window. Every night, while I'm reading. Thin them out, and I'll give you my full attention and the second half of this thing.
sp_ledger_cipher.accept_text: The risen husks in the back plots. They come to the window while I'm reading.
sp_ledger_cipher.turn_in_text:
[He has not moved from the desk, but the shutters are open for the first time.]

That's better. That's a great deal better.

Now. Sit down and tell me about the seals in the mansion, and I'll tell you what the back half of this ledger is actually counting. You are not going to care for it.

etc_descend.description:
Boneward Calder, and that title used to be a joke. Ysolde sent word, so you know roughly what's under the cult's farm.

I'll say it plainly anyway: they dug their cellar into a body. A Scourge Abomination, dead a long while, and so large that its SPINE is a corridor. You can walk the length of it upright. The ribs are the side chambers. The skull is at the far end and I have never been to the far end.

Before anybody commits men to this - and the Undercity will want to commit men - somebody has to walk it and come back with a length. Not an impression. A length, and what's in it.

Go down the spine. Come back up it.
etc_descend.accept_text: Down through the cult's cellar, into the spine. Walk it and come back.
etc_descend.turn_in_text:
That far. You're certain.

I'd written 'a cellar' in two reports. I'm going to have to go back and amend both, and I'm going to have to explain why the amendment is the size it is.

etc_warriors.description:
Now that we know how far it runs, we can talk about what's walking in it.

Scourge Warriors, in the rib tunnels, in loose patrols - and loose is the word. They don't sleep, they don't tire, and they are appalling at hiding, which has been my only advantage down there. You hear them a corridor away.

The trouble with a thing that never tires is that it doesn't need to be good. It just needs to still be there when you aren't. I've watched a pair of them walk the same rib for three days without stopping.

Break the patrols. I want a stretch of that corridor that stays empty for an hour.
etc_warriors.accept_text: In the rib tunnels, in loose patrols. You'll hear them before you see them.
etc_warriors.turn_in_text:
An hour of empty corridor. I'll take it down to the next rib and set a lamp.

That's the first ground anyone's held under that farm.

etc_ghouls.description:
Different problem, same tunnels, and this one's faster.

The ghouls came down with the Scourge originally. They had no reason to stay once it stopped - and they stayed, because the cult's plague cellar is down here and the cult leaves things out.

So they're fed. A fed ghoul pack is not the scattered, starving thing you've met out on the glades; they're fast, they hunt properly, and they travel together and turn together.

Don't let them get behind you in the ribs. There's no behind you in a corridor until suddenly there is.
etc_ghouls.accept_text: Through the ribs. They travel in packs and they turn together.
etc_ghouls.turn_in_text:
Good. The feeding's what keeps the numbers up - cut the pack down and the cellar can only grow it back so fast.

Which brings us rather neatly to the cellar.

etc_runes.description:
Here's the part I've been building to, and it's the reason I'm a Boneward and not a gravedigger.

The Scourge necromancers cut their wards into black stone. Shards of it, and they're all through the bones - and it isn't decoration. The same wards are what's HOLDING the Abomination's skeleton in the shape of a skeleton. That thing has been dead for years and it has not fallen in on itself, and the shards are why.

I want a handful. Not to break them in place, which would drop a corridor on us. To learn how they're cut, so that when we do break them we break them in an order somebody chose.

Take them off the necromancers. They'll be carrying spares.
etc_runes.accept_text: Off the necromancers in the ribs. They carry spares.
etc_runes.turn_in_text:
[He lays them out and turns each one to the lamp.]

They're sequenced. Look - this edge continues that one. It's not a ward repeated, it's a ward WRITTEN, and it runs the length of the body.

Which means there's a last one. And a last one can be first, if you walk it backwards.

etc_abomination.description:
The skull, then. And what's wired into it.

The Abomination is at the head of the spine, and the cult has run their rune stones straight into it - that's what the whole farm has been doing up there, all those calling hours in the yard. Not summoning anything. FEEDING something that was already here.

Take the necromancers off it first; they're the ones keeping the wards lit, and while the wards are lit you'll be hitting a thing that cannot be allowed to fall over.

Then put it down, and the cellar goes back to being a cellar, and this hill goes back to being a hill with an unfortunate history instead of one with a future.
etc_abomination.accept_text: In the skull, at the head of the spine. The necromancers keep the wards lit.
etc_abomination.turn_in_text:
[The lamp flames are standing straight up for the first time since he lit them.]

It's just bone now. A very large amount of ordinary bone.

I'm going to spend the rest of my career telling people that was a cellar, and every one of them is going to believe me, and that will be the correct outcome.

etc_krag.description:
There's a pit west of the ribs and I'd like it emptied before it becomes somebody's problem on a day I'm not here.

Ghoulmaster Krag keeps his pack in it. Bone-lined - he's built the thing, lined it out properly, and he feeds them on what the cult leaves behind, which is how you get a pack that size this far from anything living.

He doesn't fight at the front. He sends them and he watches how it goes and then he adjusts, and I have watched him adjust, and I did not enjoy it.

Break the pack where it lives. Then him.
etc_krag.accept_text: The bone-lined pit, west of the ribs. He sends the pack and watches.
etc_krag.turn_in_text:
Pit's cold.

That's the thing I'd have been most worried about if we'd come back in a year. A pack with a keeper is a garrison; a pack without one is just hungry.

etc_orvyn.description:
East of the ribs, in the side chamber with the light coming out of it. That's the laboratory.

Plaguemaster Orvyn runs it. The vats in there are where the blight on the Solliden fields comes from, and the Balnir paddock, and every field between here and Brill that won't take a crop - it isn't old plague lingering, it's being MADE, down here, to a recipe, on a schedule.

His acolytes work the vats and they'll defend them before they defend him, which tells you what he's taught them to value.

I want the vats cold and I want the man who wrote the recipe to stop being available for consultation.
etc_orvyn.accept_text: The lit side chamber east of the ribs. His acolytes guard the vats.
etc_orvyn.turn_in_text:
Cold vats.

I'll get word to the farms. Not that it fixes their fields - three years of that going into the soil doesn't lift because we turned a tap off. But it stops getting worse, and I've not been able to offer anybody up there a sentence like that one.

etc_formula.description:
A sheaf of stained notes, pulled off the Plaguemaster's belt and still smelling of the vat room.

It's a working document rather than a treatise: dosages scratched out and rewritten, ingredient lists with suppliers against them, timings for the pour. There's a diagram on the last sheet showing how the delivery vats feed up into the field channels above, drawn by somebody who understood plumbing better than theology.

Someone who knows reagents could learn a great deal from this - what went into those fields, and whether anything undoes it.

Assistant Grael, at the Brill Apothecary, would know what he was looking at.
etc_formula.accept_text: Take the notes to Assistant Grael at the Brill Apothecary.
etc_formula.turn_in_text:
[Grael goes very quiet, which for him is remarkable.]

This is a RECIPE. With suppliers on it. Half of these reagents came through Brill, and two of them came through this building.

I'm going to have to tell the Apothecary something, and I'm going to have to decide tonight how much of it. Thank you - I think. Ask me again in a week.
